## [2026-11-27](../../../reports/2026/11/2026-11-27.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Mass Spec Skills: Tool-Grounded Molecular Identification with Lightweight Agents](<https://deepmind.google/blog/interpreting-mass-spectra-with-google-antigravity/>)

Mass Spec Skills packages established spectral-search, formula-inference and molecular-validation tools into reusable workflows that a language-model agent can combine and explain. On 100 spectra whose compounds occur in public reference libraries, the authors report about 97% exact identification across lightweight and frontier models with fewer generated tokens, making this a useful example of improving agents through reliable tools rather than model scale alone.

**Published:** 2026-11-25 · **First seen:** 2026-11-27T11:04:25.833+00:00 · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Scientific Agents, Tool Use, Reusable Skills, Evaluation

[Blog](<https://deepmind.google/blog/interpreting-mass-spectra-with-google-antigravity/>) · [Project](<https://antigravity.google/>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. Read the complete official technical post, including the end-to-end negative-ion example, the library-covered benchmark, and limitations; directly viewed the original Figure5a/5b SVGs after lossless rasterization. The workflow chains matchms cleaning, GNPS/MoNA library search, SIRIUS formula inference, MAGMa/MetFrag fragment scoring, PubChem candidates, and RDKit validity checks. Its illustrative end-to-end run disables library lookup and shows why equal matched intensity is insufficient: the verified molecule and rejected isomers all explain97.7% of summed intensity, so chemical connectivity and diagnostic neutral losses distinguish them. This single worked example is not the benchmark. The separate controlled benchmark samples100 Enamine REAL spectra in MoNA with structures in PubChem, filters under-fragmented recordings, and runs three attempts per spectrum per setup with Gemini3.8Flash, Gemini4Argon and Gemini4Carbon. No-internet/no-skills accuracy is below4%; internet-plus-skills reaches roughly97% for all three. Figures5a/5b display means and95% intervals; timeouts over one hour are failures, while transient infrastructure/quota errors are excluded. Generated tokens fall relative to internet-only tooling by nearly fourfold for Flash, half for Argon and nearly a fifth for Carbon; these are generated-token comparisons, not end-to-end cost or latency speedups. Delayed discovery for November27: original article metadata dates publication November25 17:00UTC, while the currently inspected version has a November26 11:24UTC modification timestamp, after the November26 report cutoff. No earlier version diff is available, so current quantitative content is not projected back into the November26 window. The original publication date is retained within the November27 72-hour discovery window; this is not a claimed new November27 scientific update. The official application entry point resolves successfully, but no standalone MassSpecSkills source-code or raw benchmark release is linked or claimed here.

**Limitations:** The quantitative study measures retrieval and verification for a filtered100-compound, library-covered population, not discovery of genuinely unknown molecular structures. Three attempts per spectrum are repeated measurements, not300 independent compounds. Library membership and candidate database coverage are central; many isomers and mirror-image molecules cannot be distinguished from tandem spectra alone and require other measurements. The case study does not establish general de-novo identification accuracy. Transient infrastructure/quota failures are excluded and raw denominators, code, prompts and numeric trial data are not released in the inspected post, limiting independent reproducibility and uncertainty auditing. Skills combine multiple changes, so the comparison does not isolate each tool or reasoning component. No experiments were executed.

### [SheetAlign: Grounded Interaction and Stage-Isolated Learning for Spreadsheet Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26069>)

SheetAlign grounds spreadsheet transformations in task-specific workbook observations and API references, trains generation and review policies separately with edit-progress feedback, and selects candidates by agreement between resulting workbooks. Its small-model study shows how targeted inspection and execution checks can improve spreadsheet editing, while the four-candidate version trades additional inference work for higher final accuracy.

The four-candidate variant samples two common and two generation-policy programs, groups deterministic stored-workbook fingerprints, selects the first member of the largest agreeing group of at least two, then reviews once. No agreement falls back to the first inspectable result. Tables1/2 report SpreadsheetBench average accuracy13.5% for the base model,29.2% for the training-free grounded interface,30.4% with learning and32.8% with K=4 consistency; Domain-Spreadsheet is24.9/26.2/30.1% for those three stages. Table5 keeps K=4 fixed when comparing selection:32.8% versus30.7% first-valid and31.4% learned selection on SpreadsheetBench. Evaluation recalculates formulas using Windows Excel, whereas candidate fingerprints compare stored formula expressions without recalculation. Original cs.CL NEW membership in the Friday20 batch plus the official schedule supports an inferred November20 01:00UTC announcement while retaining the November19 receipt. This is a delayed selection within the72-hour lookback; the prior successful November20 SE NEW completion is the earliest actual catalog discovery, preserved with raw bytes/receipt. That SE cross-list supplies discovery provenance, not original-announcement evidence. The paper promises a future code release; no accessible author implementation/project was verified and none is claimed.

**Limitations:** There are unresolved numerical inconsistencies: p.6 prose says29.5% while Table1/abstract/conclusion say29.2%; p.7 prose says29.7% while Table4 says29.3%; claimed inspection/API ablation deltas6.7/3.2 points disagree with Table3 arithmetic29.2−21.4=7.8 and29.2−25.2=4.0. Three random evaluation seeds are reported, but three independently trained policy replicas are not established; most tables omit uncertainty. The final K=4 result includes additional generations, repairs and review and is not a one-sample or compute-matched Pass@1 comparison. Published external baselines differ in models, harnesses and tool access. The study is one4B backbone and two benchmarks; target regions are task-provided and correctness checks only the specified normalized target cells, not all workbook semantics or collateral edits. Fingerprints are bounded to200,000 cells/64MiB and compare stored formulas without evaluating them, so agreement is not semantic correctness. ## [2026-11-20](../../../reports/2026/11/2026-11-20.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25043>)

This laboratory-agent architecture routes proposed measurements through researcher-approved campaign settings and deterministic instrument services, while preserving records that connect each result to the next decision. A real chromatography–mass-spectrometry campaign and archived-data replays show how these controls can support agent-directed measurement selection and analysis. The demonstration covers one plate, and an operator changed approved limits outside the formal approval workflow, exposing a remaining governance gap.

Project-scoped records and a persistent per-well ledger feed an agent that proposes a measurement; the submission path checks execution controls, campaign state, method, wells and budget before the instrument sidecar checks ownership, queue and device state. A deterministic watcher stages completed evidence and starts a new turn. The live campaign used a human-prepared28-well plate and465main-room tool calls, with12operational requests refused/deferred; all wells were eventually measured at the operator’s instruction. The controlled selection evaluation is instead23archived-data campaigns using Claude Opus5, with one or three runs at each injection budget. At budgets8–24 the best well was typically measured around injection7, versus14.5 expected under a random ordering of28wells; all tested campaigns with budget≥8 identified it, but the single budget28run reached it at injection21. No fresh chemistry was run in these replays. The architecture is useful as an inspectable integration of authorization, deterministic measurement services and persistent state, not as invention of those individual mechanisms. No matching public agent implementation or raw campaign-trace release was verified. Original manuscript receipt dates are preserved. Both appear in the original Friday November20 cs.AI NEW batch and dated RECENT header. The official Wednesday14:00–Thursday14:00 Eastern window announces Thursday20:00EST, implying November20 01:00UTC public availability; this is an announcement-schedule inference, not an observed exact public visibility instant. The laboratory paper was received November18 19:00:10UTC, ten seconds after the Wednesday14:00EST boundary; Seer was received November19 17:03:24UTC. Actual first\_seen is the earliest completed successful matching team catalog: own cs.AI RECENT at November20 16:15:37.304680UTC, one millisecond before own NEW; Infra verified neither ID occurs in its earlier six catalogs, and Recipe’s matching discovery was later. **Limitations:** One reaction system, one instrument workflow and one physical campaign; humans prepared samples, approved operation and later forced exhaustive well coverage. No synthesis or sample-preparation autonomy is demonstrated. Only the replay uses controlled injection budgets; random ordering is an analytical reference rather than an equal-information comparison with informed heuristics or Bayesian optimization. Each budget has at most three campaigns, and expensive20/28budgets have one. The12refusals out of465tool calls are operational events, not an adversarial attack success rate. E-stop/Stop and a pause-review-resume intervention were not exercised. An operator raised the live budget20→30 by directly editing the campaign record outside approval, so immutable approved limits are not established. Checks regulate instrument operations, not chemical hazards. Each condition has one reaction well; independent integrations support the strongest condition but closely ranked oxidants are not statistically separable. Logged replay reasoning adds10–24minutes for budgets8–24; the assumed15minutes/injection is not a general wall-time or cost advantage. OpenAI reports model-assisted circuit rewrites and compares optimizing existing processor RTL with building a core from a written specification. **Published:** 2026-11-18 · **First seen:** 2026-11-19T11:08:04.665+00:00 · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Hardware Agents, Tool Verification, RTL Optimization

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. Complete November18 technical article inspected. Its new evaluation includes 9,881 scored runs across two 32-bit RISC-V cores, two tasks and multiple token budgets. Valid designs receive normalized throughput from hidden-workload instructions per cycle and Yosys-estimated clock frequency; failures or area above16× baseline score zero. Separate production-block area and AMD PPA claims are author reports, not the same benchmark or newly released silicon evidence.

**Limitations:** Simulation tests do not prove full functional equivalence. A loose16× area cap and omission of original features can favor specification-built designs; physical timing checks are deferred. Scores normalize to the best observed throughput and average over failures, rather than measuring a universal chip speedup. Matching author evaluation code, uncertainty estimates and the proprietary design artifacts were not supplied in the inspected article.
